title: Nasdaq Rallies 1.6% as CoreWeave Fuels a Tech Close on a Bond-Free Veterans Day
dek: The S&P 500 closed at 7,619.38 and the Nasdaq Composite at 25,466.19 as AI infrastructure stocks led, though the Nasdaq gave back part of its midday gain. The bond market stayed shut.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Black-and-white photograph of an automatic ticker apparatus on the New York Stock Exchange trading floor
image.credit: Library of Congress via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: The S&P 500 rose 1.3% to 7,619.38, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.5% to 52,486.49 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.6% to 25,466.19 (AP).
For the week, the S&P 500 is up 3.3% and the Nasdaq up 3.6%; the Russell 2000 rose 0.9% to 2,846.26 on the day (AP).
The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ closed 2.31% higher, against 1.30% for the S&P 500 fund SPY and 0.49% for the Dow fund DIA; tech gave back part of a larger midday gain (StockTitan, citing CNBC).
CoreWeave closed up 24.71% and Nvidia 2.87%; memory and photonics names led, with Sandisk up 16% and Micron up 13% (StockTitan and CNBC).
The US bond market was closed for Veterans Day under SIFMA's recommendation, so Tuesday's 10-year Treasury close of 4.98% remains the last Treasury reading (SIFMA; CNN Business).
body:
US stocks closed higher on Wednesday, Veterans Day, in a session with stock exchanges open and the bond market shut. The S&P 500 rose 1.3% to 7,619.38, its gain carrying it to within 2.6% of the record it set last month, according to the Associated Press.

## Where the indexes closed

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 254.60 points, or 0.5%, to 52,486.49. The Nasdaq Composite rose 400.31 points, or 1.6%, to 25,466.19, and the Russell 2000 of smaller companies rose 0.9% to 2,846.26. The Nasdaq had been up about 2% at midday, so the close showed some fading into the afternoon.

## Sectors and the AI trade

Technology did most of the work. The Nasdaq 100 fund closed 2.31% higher, well ahead of the Dow fund's 0.49% gain, according to StockTitan. CNBC reported that Sandisk and Micron advanced 16% and 13%, and that photonics names Coherent and Lumentum rose 12% and 14%. The AI-focused iShares ETF gained 7%.

Microsoft fell 2% for a second day after Anthropic unveiled AI workplace tools that could compete with core Office products, CNBC reported.

## Movers

CoreWeave closed 24.71% higher after reporting third-quarter revenue above estimates and raising its full-year guidance. Azenta rose 22% after a fiscal fourth-quarter beat and a revenue outlook above consensus. Corning gained more than 10% after Jefferies initiated coverage with a buy rating. Oklo rose about 6% after the Energy Department cleared its Groves-1 test reactor for unrestricted operations. Six Flags rose 8% on a large insider purchase by a director.

## What is still open

The bond market will not reopen until Thursday, when the first clean Treasury reaction to the hot October CPI report arrives. Markets still price a quarter-point hike at the December meeting as the base case, per CME FedWatch data cited by CNN and CNBC. Nebius reports third-quarter results before the open on Thursday, the next test of the AI-infrastructure rally.

marketImpact.summary: The rally is concentrated in AI infrastructure and memory names. It lifted indexes, but the bond market's silence means the rate-hike question is still unresolved until Thursday.
marketImpact.timeframe: Veterans Day close, then Thursday's Treasury reopening and Nebius results

Micron rose about 13% in a memory-chip rebound (CNBC)
Fell 2% for a second day after Anthropic's workplace-tools launch (CNBC)
Reports before the open Thursday; shares rose sharply early Wednesday on the CoreWeave read-through
